concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: یہ دوسروں کو گمراہ کرنے کی سنگینی کو ظاہر کرتا ہے - جوابدہی اپنے گناہوں سے آگے بڑھ کر متاثرین تک پہنچتی ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: سيطلب أهل النار عذاباً مضاعفاً لمن أضلهم، طالبين عذاباً مضاعفاً في النار.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: يُظهر هذا خطورة إضلال الآخرين - المساءلة تمتد إلى ما وراء خطايا المرء لتشمل من تأثروا سلباً.

concepts.title: Regret and Blame
concepts.coreInsight: In the Fire, people will turn against each other in blame, seeking to identify who brought this suffering upon them.
concepts.whyItMatters: Hellfire destroys all bonds and loyalty - even former companions become sources of mutual hatred and blame.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: آگ میں لوگ ایک دوسرے کو الزام دیں گے، یہ تلاش کرتے ہوئے کہ انہیں یہ عذاب کس نے دلوایا۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: جہنم تمام تعلقات اور وفاداری کو ختم کر دیتی ہے - سابقہ ساتھی بھی باہمی نفرت کا ذریعہ بن جاتے ہیں۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: في النار، سيلوم الناس بعضهم البعض، محاولين تحديد من جلب عليهم هذا العذاب.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: نار جهنم تدمر جميع الروابط والولاء - حتى الرفاق السابقون يصبحون مصدر كراهية ولوم متبادل.

concepts.title: Plea to Lord
concepts.coreInsight: Even in Hell, the condemned still address Allah as 'Our Lord' (Rabbana), acknowledging His sovereignty in their misery.
concepts.whyItMatters: This demonstrates that divine lordship is absolute - even the damned cannot deny Allah's authority over them.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: جہنم میں بھی مجرم اللہ کو 'ہمارے رب' (ربنا) کہہ کر پکارتے ہیں، اپنی بدحالی میں اس کی حاکمیت کو تسلیم کرتے ہوئے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: یہ ظاہر کرتا ہے کہ الہی حاکمیت مطلق ہے - حتیٰ کہ معذب بھی اللہ کی اتھارٹی سے انکار نہیں کر سکتے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: حتى في جهنم، يخاطب المعذبون الله بـ'ربنا'، مقرّين بسيادته في شقائهم.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: يُظهر هذا أن الربوبية الإلهية مطلقة - حتى المعذبون لا يستطيعون إنكار سلطة الله عليهم.

concepts.title: Fire's Reality
concepts.coreInsight: The Fire (al-Nar) is presented as the ultimate destination and reality for the rejecters, a place of conscious suffering.
concepts.whyItMatters: Hell is not metaphorical - it is a real place of torment where people remain aware and experience ongoing regret.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: آگ (النار) کو منکرین کی حتمی منزل اور حقیقت کے طور پر پیش کیا گیا ہے، شعوری عذاب کی جگہ۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: جہنم تمثیلی نہیں - یہ عذاب کی حقیقی جگہ ہے جہاں لوگ باشعور رہتے اور مسلسل پچھتاوا محسوس کرتے ہیں۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: تُقدَّم النار كمصير نهائي وحقيقة للمنكرين، مكان العذاب الواعي.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: جهنم ليست استعارة - إنها مكان حقيقي للعذاب حيث يبقى الناس واعين ويختبرون ندماً مستمراً.

61.layer4: Both Shia and Sunni scholars agree that this verse establishes the principle of proportional responsibility in divine justice. Ibn Kathir and Qurtubi, prominent Sunni exegetes, explain that misleaders face double punishment because they sinned themselves and caused others to sin. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi adds that the request for increased punishment demonstrates the psychological state of Hell's inhabitants, consumed by anger and regret. Where Shia and Sunni interpretations diverge is in applying this principle to leadership disputes in Islamic history. Shia scholars like Tabatabai see this verse as validating the importance of following divinely appointed leadership, arguing that those who deviated from the Ahlul Bayt's guidance led the community into various forms of misguidance, whose consequences persist. Sunni scholars generally interpret the verse more broadly, applying it to any false religious or worldly leadership. Both traditions emphasize that blind following (taqlid) in matters of belief is impermissible. However, Shia jurisprudence permits taqlid of qualified mujtahids in legal matters while requiring independent investigation in theological principles, reflecting a nuanced understanding of when following authority is appropriate versus when it constitutes the kind of blind following condemned in this verse.
61.layer4_urdu: شیعہ اور سنی دونوں علماء اس بات پر متفق ہیں کہ یہ آیت الہی انصاف میں متناسب ذمہ داری کا اصول قائم کرتی ہے۔ ابن کثیر اور قرطبی، نامور سنی مفسرین، وضاحت کرتے ہیں کہ گمراہ کرنے والوں کو دوہری سزا کا سامنا ہے کیونکہ انہوں نے خود گناہ کیا اور دوسروں کو گناہ کرنے کا سبب بنایا۔ فخر الدین رازی کہتے ہیں کہ بڑھی ہوئی سزا کی درخواست جہنم کے باشندوں کی نفسیاتی حالت کو ظاہر کرتی ہے، غصے اور ندامت میں مبتلا۔ جہاں شیعہ اور سنی تشریحات مختلف ہیں وہ اس اصول کو مخصوص تاریخی شخصیات پر لاگو کرنے میں ہے، شیعہ روایات خاص طور پر ان لوگوں کی مذمت کرتی ہیں جنہوں نے اہل بیت کی امامت سے انکار کیا اور اموی حکمرانی کو جائز ٹھہرایا۔
61.layer4_ar: يتفق علماء الشيعة والسنة على أن هذه الآية تُرسي مبدأ التناسب في المسؤولية ضمن منظومة العدل الإلهي. فيُبيِّن كل من ابن كثير والقرطبي أن المضلِّلين يستحقون عذاباً مضاعفاً لأنهم أذنبوا وأوقعوا سواهم في الذنب. ويُضيف فخر الدين الرازي أن هذا الطلب يكشف الحالة النفسية لأهل النار، وهم في دوامة من الغضب والحسرة. وتفترق الرؤيتان الشيعية والسنية في تطبيق هذا المبدأ على الخلافات التاريخية في القيادة؛ إذ يرى علماء الشيعة كالطباطبائي أن الآية تُسبغ مشروعيةً على أهمية اتِّباع القيادة الإلهية المعيَّنة، وأن من حادوا عن هدي أهل البيت عليهم السلام أوقعوا الأمة في أشكال شتى من الضلال ستتبيَّن تبعاتها. في حين يُفسِّر علماء السنة الآية بمفهوم أوسع يشمل كل قيادة دينية أو دنيوية زائفة. غير أن التراثين معاً يشدِّدان على تحريم التقليد الأعمى في مسائل العقيدة. وتُجيز الفقه الشيعي تقليد المجتهدين المؤهَّلين في المسائل الفقهية مع إيجاب الاستقلال في الأصول الاعتقادية، في نظرة رشيدة تُفرِّق بين اتِّباع العالِم المشروع والتبعية العمياء المذمومة التي تجلوها هذه الآية.
61.layer1: Verse 61 continues the vivid Quranic scene of the people of Hellfire engaged in mutual blame and cursing. After the followers had turned on their leaders in verse 60, declaring that it was those very leaders who brought them to their wretched fate, they now address Allah directly in a plea laced with bitterness and indignation. They cry out: 'Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us - increase for him double punishment in the Fire.' This supplication is remarkable because it comes from people who are already suffering the most severe torment imaginable, yet they are so consumed by rage at those who misled them that they actively petition Allah for an even greater punishment to be inflicted on the ringleaders of their misguidance. The Arabic phrase 'man qaddama lana hadha' literally means 'whoever forwarded this to us' or 'prepared this for us,' indicating that they view their condition in Hell as something deliberately engineered for them by those who led them astray. This verse serves as a powerful warning to all believers about the grave responsibility that comes with influencing others. Those who mislead people away from faith, whether through ideological corruption, bad companionship, or promoting sinful culture, will bear not only their own punishment but will also be cursed by the very people they led to ruin. The practical lesson is clear: we must be extremely cautious about who we follow, what ideologies we embrace, and what kind of influence we exert over others. Blind following of leaders and thinkers without examining whether their guidance aligns with divine revelation can have consequences that last into eternity.
61.layer2: Imam Tabari in his Jami al-Bayan records multiple chains of narration regarding this verse, noting that the followers are addressing Allah with this prayer of condemnation against those who misled them. Tabari draws a direct parallel with Surah Al-Araf 7:38, where Allah describes a similar scenario: when each group enters the Fire, it curses the one that preceded it, until when they are all gathered together, the last of them says to the first: 'Our Lord, these misled us, so give them a double punishment in the Fire.' Allah responds there by saying that each will receive double, but they do not know. Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim elaborates on the significance of the word 'adiban difa' meaning a doubled torment. He explains that the followers' request for double punishment for their leaders reflects the Islamic principle that those who establish evil practices bear the sin of that evil itself as well as the sin of all who follow them in it, as the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said: 'Whoever introduces an evil practice in Islam, he will bear its sin and the sin of those who act upon it, without their burden being reduced in the least.' This hadith, recorded in Sahih Muslim, gives scholarly weight to understanding why the people of Hell make this specific plea. Imam Qurtubi in his Al-Jami li-Ahkam al-Quran notes that this verse reveals the absolute futility of misplaced loyalty. In the world, people often excuse leaders of falsehood or follow them blindly, but in the Hereafter all such pretenses dissolve and only the reality of who led whom to destruction remains. The supplication is not granted in the sense of reducing the followers' punishment; rather, it functions as a testament to the justice of Allah in assigning responsibility.
61.layer3: Wahbah al-Zuhayli in his Al-Tafsir al-Munir situates this verse within the broader rhetorical strategy of Surah Sad, which uses contrasting scenes of paradise and hell to awaken the human conscience. He notes that the plea of the followers in Hell against their leaders is psychologically and spiritually significant because it reveals how the social architecture of corruption in this world is dismantled in the Hereafter. Those who commanded prestige, influence, and mass following on earth are now the objects of the most intense curses and resentment from those very same followers. Sayyid Qutb in his Fi Zilal al-Quran reflects that this verse is a scene of stark emotional power that the Quran uses to strip away all illusions about the ultimate value of worldly leadership built on falsehood. He writes that on that Day, no amount of charisma, rhetoric, or social power will shield anyone from accountability. The followers' cry of 'increase for him double punishment' is a declaration of the complete collapse of the bond of falsehood that united them in the world. Ibn Uthaymeen, in his commentary on related verses, emphasizes that this should instill in every Muslim a deep sense of personal accountability for whom they follow. The contemporary relevance is profound: in an era of social media influencers, celebrity scholars of dubious credentials, and political ideologues who promote ideas contrary to Quran and Sunnah, every Muslim must exercise critical discernment. The ease with which millions follow without scrutiny echoes the dynamic condemned in this verse. Following someone who leads you away from truth carries eternal consequences, and those who are misled will find no sympathy from their former leaders on the Day of Judgment.

concepts.title: Missing Believers
concepts.coreInsight: The people of Hell will wonder about the believers they once mocked and considered evil - why can't they see them in Hell?
concepts.whyItMatters: This reveals the inverted reality of the Hereafter - those deemed 'worst' in worldly eyes are actually saved, while the arrogant are damned.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: جہنمی ان مومنوں کے بارے میں حیران ہوں گے جن کا وہ مذاق اڑاتے اور انہیں بُرا سمجھتے تھے - وہ جہنم میں کیوں نظر نہیں آتے؟
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: یہ آخرت کی الٹی حقیقت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے - جنہیں دنیا میں 'بدترین' سمجھا گیا وہ درحقیقت محفوظ ہیں، جبکہ مغرور لوگ معذب ہیں۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: سيتساءل أهل النار عن المؤمنين الذين سخروا منهم واعتبروهم أشراراً - لماذا لا يرونهم في جهنم؟
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: يكشف هذا عن الواقع المعكوس للآخرة - الذين اعتُبروا 'أسوأ' في نظر الدنيا نجوا فعلياً، بينما المتكبرون معذبون.

concepts.title: Worldly Judgment
concepts.coreInsight: The damned had counted believers among 'the worst' (al-ashrar), showing how worldly standards of good and evil are often inverted.
concepts.whyItMatters: Material success and social status in this world are poor indicators of spiritual rank - humility and faith matter most.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: معذبین نے مومنوں کو 'بدترین' (الاشرار) میں شمار کیا تھا، یہ ظاہر کرتے ہوئے کہ کس طرح دنیوی معیارات اکثر الٹے ہوتے ہیں۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: اس دنیا میں مادی کامیابی اور سماجی حیثیت روحانی مقام کے ناقص اشارے ہیں - عاجزی اور ایمان سب سے زیادہ اہم ہیں۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: اعتبر المعذبون المؤمنين من 'الأشرار'، مما يُظهر كيف أن معايير الخير والشر الدنيوية غالباً ما تكون معكوسة.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: النجاح المادي والمكانة الاجتماعية في هذا العالم مؤشرات ضعيفة للمرتبة الروحية - التواضع والإيمان هما الأهم.

concepts.title: Regretful Question
concepts.coreInsight: This questioning reveals deep regret and confusion - the rejecters realize their terrible misjudgment too late.
concepts.whyItMatters: In the Hereafter, all illusions are stripped away and reality becomes painfully clear - but it's too late for change.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: یہ سوال گہرے افسوس اور الجھن کو ظاہر کرتا ہے - منکرین اپنی خوفناک غلط فہمی کو بہت دیر سے سمجھتے ہیں۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: آخرت میں تمام فریب دور ہو جاتے ہیں اور حقیقت تکلیف دہ طور پر واضح ہو جاتی ہے - لیکن تبدیلی کے لیے بہت دیر ہو چکی ہوتی ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: يكشف هذا السؤال عن ندم وحيرة عميقين - يدرك المنكرون سوء حكمهم الرهيب بعد فوات الأوان.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: في الآخرة، تتلاشى جميع الأوهام ويصبح الواقع واضحاً بشكل مؤلم - لكن فات الأوان للتغيير.

62.layer4: Sunni and Shia commentators largely agree on the basic interpretation of this verse, that the disbelievers are shocked not to find the believers in Hell with them. Ibn Kathir explains that the verse refers to the poor Muslims whom the Quraysh aristocracy mocked, such as Bilal, Ammar, and Suhayb. Qurtubi adds that it demonstrates the reversal of worldly and eternal values. Razi emphasizes that the verse proves worldly status is not an indicator of spiritual rank. The Shia perspective adds a specific historical dimension regarding the Ahlul Bayt and their followers. Tabatabai and other Shia scholars note that throughout history, the followers of the Ahlul Bayt were often marginalized, persecuted, and viewed with contempt by ruling powers and their supporters. Yet these same persecutors will be shocked in the Hereafter to find that those they despised have achieved eternal salvation while they face eternal punishment. This interpretation extends the verse's application from the Prophet's era to the entire subsequent history of Islam. Both traditions emphasize the importance of not judging people by worldly standards and of defending the oppressed even when they lack worldly power. The consensus is that true wisdom lies in recognizing that divine values differ fundamentally from worldly values.
62.layer4_urdu: سنی اور شیعہ مفسرین بڑی حد تک اس آیت کی بنیادی تشریح پر متفق ہیں کہ کافر حیران ہیں کہ مومنین کو جہنم میں اپنے ساتھ نہیں پاتے۔ ابن کثیر وضاحت کرتے ہیں کہ آیت ان غریب مسلمانوں کی طرف اشارہ کرتی ہے جن کا قریش کی اشرافیہ نے مذاق اڑایا، جیسے بلال، عمار اور صہیب۔ قرطبی کہتے ہیں کہ یہ دنیاوی اور ابدی اقدار کے الٹ پھیر کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ رازی اس بات پر زور دیتے ہیں کہ آیت ثابت کرتی ہے کہ دنیاوی حیثیت روحانی درجے کا اشارہ نہیں ہے۔ شیعہ نقطہ نظر ایک خاص جہت شامل کرتا ہے: یہ آیت خاص طور پر اہل بیت کے پیروکاروں پر لاگو ہوتی ہے جنہیں تاریخ میں ظلم اور حقارت کا سامنا رہا۔
62.layer4_ar: يتفق مفسِّرو الشيعة والسنة إجمالاً على تفسير هذه الآية بأنها تصوير لدهشة الكافرين من خلوِّ النار من المؤمنين الذين كانوا يُصنِّفونهم «أشراراً». فيُبيِّن ابن كثير أن الآية تُشير إلى فقراء المسلمين الذين سخرت منهم أرستقراطية قريش كبلال وعمار وصهيب. ويضيف القرطبي أنها تُجسِّد انقلاب القيم الدنيوية والأخروية رأساً على عقب. ويُشدِّد الرازي على أن الآية تُثبت أن المكانة الدنيوية ليست مقياساً للمنزلة الروحية. وتُضيف الرؤية الشيعية بُعداً تاريخياً خاصاً يتصل بأهل البيت عليهم السلام وشيعتهم؛ فيُلاحِظ الطباطبائي وسواه من علماء الشيعة أن أتباع أهل البيت على مرِّ التاريخ كثيراً ما هُمِّشوا واضطُهِدوا وقُوبلوا بازدراء الحكام المتسلِّطين وأعوانهم. غير أن هؤلاء المضطهِدين أنفسهم سيصطدمون في الآخرة بمفاجأة موجعة حين يجدون أن من كانوا يزدرونهم قد نالوا الخلاص الأبدي بينما هم يواجهون العذاب الدائم. ويمتدُّ هذا التفسير بتطبيق مضمون الآية من عصر النبي إلى سائر تاريخ الإسلام. ويتفق التراثان على ضرورة ألا يُحكَم على الناس بمعايير الدنيا وعلى واجب نصرة المستضعفين حتى حين يفتقرون إلى القوة الدنيوية. والمقرَّر لديهما أن الحكمة الحقيقية تكمن في إدراك أن القيم الإلهية تختلف جذرياً عن القيم الدنيوية.
62.layer1: In verse 62, the scene in Hellfire deepens and takes an unexpected turn. The people in the Fire suddenly pause from their mutual recriminations and ask a bewildered question: 'Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the worst?' This verse is striking because it reveals a moment of genuine confusion among the inhabitants of Hell. They had expected to see certain people - those they had ridiculed, mocked, and despised in the worldly life - sharing in their torment. These were the believers, the followers of the Prophet, the poor and weak Muslims who had been jeered at by the powerful disbelievers of Quraysh and other communities. The Meccans had contemptuously regarded figures like Bilal, Ammar ibn Yasir, Suhayb, and Khabbab - all early Muslim converts from humble backgrounds - as wretched individuals of the lowest social standing. In the arrogance of their worldly pride, they assumed that such people would certainly end up in Hell. Now, finding themselves in the Fire, they look around and cannot find these people anywhere among them. The absence is striking and disorienting. The Arabic term 'ashrar' means 'the worst' or 'the most wicked,' and it is precisely the label that the arrogant disbelievers had applied to the believing poor. This verse is a powerful lesson about the inversion of values that occurs on the Day of Judgment. Those who were despised for their faith are elevated, while those who thought themselves superior are brought low. The question the disbelievers ask is tinged with both confusion and a dawning realization of how completely their worldview was inverted.
62.layer2: Imam Tabari records from the early commentators, including Mujahid, that this verse specifically refers to the arrogant Meccan leaders looking around in Hell and wondering why they cannot find those humble Muslim believers whom they used to mock. Mujahid is reported to have said in relation to this verse: 'This is what Abu Jahl will say - he will look for Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb and others like them and not find them.' Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir elaborates on this interpretation, noting that this represents one of the great reversals of Judgment Day: those who were mocked and belittled in the world for their faith are now absent from Hell because they are in the high stations of Paradise. He draws on the Quranic principle that the arrogant of this world are the most humiliated in the next. Ibn Kathir also connects this to Surah Al-Mutaffifin 83:29-34, where Allah describes how the criminals used to laugh at the believers in the world, but on the Day of Judgment the believers will laugh at the disbelievers. Imam Qurtubi notes that the word 'ashrar' used here to describe how the disbelievers labeled the believers is significant: in their blindness, the powerful looked at the socially weak and religiously faithful and saw only worthlessness. But the reality known to Allah was the complete opposite. Al-Razi in his Mafatih al-Ghayb observes that this verse illustrates the principle that worldly criteria of judging people - wealth, social status, influence - are not divine criteria. The people of Hell used worldly lenses to assess who was righteous and who was wicked, and that fundamental error is now exposed.
62.layer3: Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran describes this moment in Hell as one of the most psychologically penetrating scenes in the entire Quran. The disbelievers, now stripped of all pretense, find themselves unable to locate the people they once despised. The question 'why do we not see them?' is simultaneously a confession and a realization: the very people they considered beneath them were actually the ones favored by Allah. Qutb writes that this verse encapsulates the great tragic irony of rejecting the truth: those who mock the bearers of truth and align themselves with worldly power find in the Hereafter that they have gambled and lost everything. Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir notes that this verse has direct contemporary relevance because the same dynamics of social mockery of the religious play out in every age. Believers who are mocked for their hijab, their prayer, their refusal to compromise their deen, or their adherence to the Sunnah may find themselves ridiculed by the culturally dominant. But the Quran assures them that the ultimate assessment belongs to Allah alone. Ibn Uthaymeen commented on related material noting that this verse should strengthen the resolve of every sincere Muslim who faces social ridicule for their faith. The worldly contempt of the powerful means nothing in the scale of divine judgment. Modern psychologists note that the need for social validation is one of the most powerful human drives, and the Quran addresses this directly by showing that the opinions of the worldly elite will mean absolutely nothing in the Hereafter - indeed, those very elites will be the ones bewildered by the absence of the people they mocked, who now reside in Paradise.

concepts.title: Mockery's Price
concepts.coreInsight: The damned question whether they made believers objects of ridicule (sikhriyya), realizing their arrogance led to their doom.
concepts.whyItMatters: Mocking faith and believers is a grave sin that can lead to eternal loss - humility before truth is essential.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: معذب سوال کرتے ہیں کہ کیا انہوں نے مومنوں کو مذاق (سخریا) کا نشانہ بنایا، یہ سمجھتے ہوئے کہ ان کا تکبر ان کی بربادی کا سبب بنا۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: ایمان اور مومنوں کا مذاق اڑانا ایک سنگین گناہ ہے جو ابدی نقصان کا باعث بن سکتا ہے - سچائی کے سامنے عاجزی ضروری ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: يتساءل المعذبون ما إذا اتخذوا المؤمنين سخرياً، مدركين أن غرورهم أدى إلى هلاكهم.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: السخرية من الإيمان والمؤمنين خطيئة جسيمة يمكن أن تؤدي إلى خسارة أبدية - التواضع أمام الحق ضروري.

concepts.title: Blinded Vision
concepts.coreInsight: They wonder if their vision (al-absar) turned away from seeing the believers, suggesting spiritual blindness in the worldly life.
concepts.whyItMatters: Arrogance blinds us to truth - those who mock the righteous fail to see their own spiritual poverty.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: وہ سوچتے ہیں کہ کیا ان کی نظر (الابصار) مومنوں کو دیکھنے سے ہٹ گئی تھی، دنیوی زندگی میں روحانی اندھا پن کی طرف اشارہ کرتے ہوئے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: تکبر ہمیں سچائی سے اندھا کر دیتا ہے - جو نیک لوگوں کا مذاق اڑاتے ہیں وہ اپنی روحانی غربت نہیں دیکھ پاتے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: يتساءلون ما إذا انحرفت أبصارهم عن رؤية المؤمنين، مما يشير إلى العمى الروحي في الحياة الدنيوية.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: الكبرياء تعمينا عن الحق - أولئك الذين يسخرون من الأبرار يفشلون في رؤية فقرهم الروحي.

concepts.title: Rhetorical Admission
concepts.coreInsight: This rhetorical question is essentially an admission of guilt - they know they mocked believers and now realize their error.
concepts.whyItMatters: In the Hereafter, self-deception is impossible - people will be forced to confront the truth they denied.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: یہ بیانیہ سوال بنیادی طور پر جرم کا اعتراف ہے - وہ جانتے ہیں کہ انہوں نے مومنوں کا مذاق اڑایا اور اب اپنی غلطی کو سمجھتے ہیں۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: آخرت میں خود فریبی ناممکن ہے - لوگوں کو اس سچائی کا سامنا کرنا پڑے گا جسے انہوں نے رد کیا تھا۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: هذا السؤال البلاغي هو في الأساس اعتراف بالذنب - يعلمون أنهم سخروا من المؤمنين ويدركون الآن خطأهم.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: في الآخرة، يستحيل خداع الذات - سيُجبر الناس على مواجهة الحق الذي أنكروه.

63.layer4: Sunni and Shia exegetes agree that this verse depicts the disbelievers' realization that they mocked those who deserved honor. Ibn Kathir explains that the verse shows their regret and confusion upon discovering the believers are in Paradise. Qurtubi notes that it demonstrates how worldly judgments are often reversed in the Hereafter. Razi emphasizes the psychological aspect, that the question form indicates internal debate and uncertainty. The Shia interpretation adds specific application to the persecution of the Ahlul Bayt and their followers. Tabatabai and other Shia scholars note that throughout Islamic history, those who remained loyal to the Ahlul Bayt often faced mockery, marginalization, and worse from the dominant powers and their supporters. The Abbasids and Umayyads promoted narratives that portrayed the Ahlul Bayt's supporters as extremists or troublemakers. This verse assures the followers of the Ahlul Bayt that such mockery will be exposed as grave error in the Hereafter. Both traditions emphasize the importance of never mocking others, especially for their religious convictions or practices. The Prophet said, 'Do not despise any Muslim, for even the lowliest of them may be more beloved to God than you.' This principle is universally accepted across Islamic schools of thought, though its application to historical conflicts differs between Shia and Sunni perspectives.
63.layer4_urdu: سنی اور شیعہ مفسرین اس بات پر متفق ہیں کہ یہ آیت کافروں کے احساس کو بیان کرتی ہے کہ انہوں نے ان لوگوں کا مذاق اڑایا جو عزت کے مستحق تھے۔ ابن کثیر وضاحت کرتے ہیں کہ آیت ان کی ندامت اور حیرانی کو دکھاتی ہے جب انہیں پتہ چلتا ہے کہ مومنین جنت میں ہیں۔ قرطبی نوٹ کرتے ہیں کہ یہ ظاہر کرتا ہے کہ کیسے دنیاوی فیصلے اکثر آخرت میں الٹ جاتے ہیں۔ رازی نفسیاتی پہلو پر زور دیتے ہیں کہ سوالیہ شکل اندرونی بحث اور غیر یقینی کی نشاندہی کرتی ہے۔ شیعہ تشریح اہل بیت کے پیروکاروں پر مخصوص اطلاق شامل کرتی ہے، جن کا تاریخ میں مذاق اڑایا گیا لیکن اللہ کے نزدیک معزز ہیں۔
63.layer4_ar: يتفق مفسِّرو السنة والشيعة على أن هذه الآية تصوِّر إدراك الكافرين المتأخِّر أنهم سخروا ممن استحقوا الإجلال. ويُبيِّن ابن كثير أن الآية تُظهر ندمهم وحيرتهم حين يكتشفون أن المؤمنين في الجنة. ويُلاحِظ القرطبي أنها تُثبت انقلاب الأحكام الدنيوية والأخروية. ويُشدِّد الرازي على الجانب النفسي مُلاحِظاً أن الاستفهام يُشير إلى نقاش داخلي وحالة من التردد واللايقين. ويُضيف التفسير الشيعي تطبيقاً تاريخياً محدَّداً يتعلق باضطهاد أهل البيت عليهم السلام وأتباعهم؛ فيُلاحِظ الطباطبائي وسواه من علماء الشيعة أن الموالين لأهل البيت على مرِّ تاريخ الإسلام واجهوا السخرية والتهميش وما هو أشد من ذلك على أيدي القوى الحاكمة ومناصريها. وتُطمئن الآية أتباع أهل البيت بأن هذه السخرية ستُفضَح يوم القيامة بوصفها خطأً جسيماً. ويتفق التراثان على حرمة السخرية من الآخرين لا سيما بسبب قناعاتهم أو ممارساتهم الدينية. وقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: «لا تحقِرنَّ من المسلمين أحداً؛ فإن صغيرهم عند الله قد يكون أعظم منك.» وهذا المبدأ مقبول بإجماع في جميع المذاهب الإسلامية وإن تفاوتت تطبيقاته على الخلافات التاريخية بين الشيعة والسنة.
63.layer1: Verse 63 continues the puzzled interrogation of the people of Hellfire as they struggle to understand why they cannot find those who they had mocked and belittled in the world. They offer two possible explanations for the absence of these believers: 'Is it because we took them in ridicule, or has our vision turned away from them?' The first possibility they raise is a dawning, agonizing realization - that perhaps the very reason they cannot see the believers is because they treated them with contempt. The Arabic word 'sikhriyan' refers to mockery, ridicule, and treating someone as a subject of jest. The disbelievers seem to begin admitting, within the confusion of their torment, that their mockery of the believers in the world may have been the very thing that separated those believers from their company in the Hereafter. The second possibility they raise - that their vision has somehow turned away from those people - is a more desperate clutching at excuses, suggesting perhaps a physical inability to see rather than accepting the moral reality. Classical scholars understand the verse as showing the disbelievers on the verge of realizing the full weight of their error: that their arrogance and mockery of the faithful was not a trivial matter but a consequential moral failure that contributed to their spiritual destruction. This verse delivers a pointed warning to anyone who makes religion or religious people the object of their ridicule. Mocking a person for their piety, their observance of Islamic practice, or their sincere devotion to Allah is a deeply serious matter with consequences that can weigh on a person's eternal fate.
63.layer2: Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim explains that the word 'sikhriyan' in this verse is the same root used in Surah Al-Mutaffifin and elsewhere, where the Quran describes how the criminals and disbelievers used to 'make a mockery' of the believers. He connects this verse to a broader Quranic theme about the sin of ridiculing the righteous. The question the disbelievers ask - 'did we take them in ridicule?' - reads in the Arabic as an interrogative that carries its own implicit admission of guilt. It is as though they are beginning to realize that their mockery in the world was the very action that sealed the separation between them and the believers in the Hereafter. Imam Tabari records that early commentators understood this verse as depicting the disbelievers coming to a painful realization about their own actions. Tabari notes that the second clause - 'or has our vision turned away from them?' - represents a desperate alternative explanation, where the disbelievers hope that perhaps it is only a matter of limited vision in Hell rather than the truth that the believers are elsewhere entirely. Imam Qurtubi draws a fiqh lesson from this verse, noting that ridicule of the people of righteousness is a major sin in Islamic law. He cites the verse alongside other Quranic evidence to establish that contempt for the faithful is an act that earns divine displeasure. Al-Razi in his Mafatih al-Ghayb notes the rhetorical beauty of the verse: the disbelievers' own question becomes a self-indictment, and the way the verse is phrased draws out the moral lesson that mockery has consequences far beyond the social.
63.layer3: Wahbah al-Zuhayli observes in Al-Tafsir al-Munir that this verse is particularly relevant in contemporary times because the culture of mockery of religious people and religious practice has never been more widespread. In the modern media landscape, religious devotion is often treated as a subject for comedy, satire, and ridicule. Muslims who practice their faith visibly - through dress, prayer, halal dietary choices, or abstention from immoral entertainment - are frequently subjected to social ridicule. The verse warns that this behavior is not without eternal consequence. Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran draws out the emotional dimension of this verse with his characteristic literary sensitivity. He notes that the disbelievers' self-questioning in Hell - 'did we take them in ridicule?' - is perhaps the most honest moment of self-reflection they ever have. In the world, they were convinced of their own superiority and the wretchedness of the believers. In Hell, they are forced to confront the possibility that their ridicule was not a sign of their cleverness but of their profound spiritual blindness. Ibn Uthaymeen, when commenting on the ethics of treating believers with contempt, would frequently reference related verses to emphasize that a Muslim must maintain respect for those who are righteous regardless of their social standing. The contemporary Muslim living in a secular society faces constant pressure to laugh along when Islam or Muslims are mocked. This verse provides a powerful reminder that joining in such ridicule - even passively - is a spiritually dangerous act. The disbelievers in Hell are not condemned merely for their doctrinal errors but for the way those errors expressed themselves in contempt for the faithful.

concepts.title: Hellfire Quarrels
concepts.coreInsight: Allah confirms that the quarreling (takhasum) of the people of Hell is absolute truth - they will indeed dispute and blame each other.
concepts.whyItMatters: Hell destroys all companionship and unity, leaving only mutual hatred and endless conflict among its inhabitants.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: اللہ تصدیق کرتا ہے کہ جہنم والوں کا جھگڑنا (تخاصم) مطلق سچائی ہے - وہ واقعی ایک دوسرے سے بحث اور الزام تراشی کریں گے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: جہنم تمام رفاقت اور اتحاد کو ختم کر دیتی ہے، صرف باہمی نفرت اور لامتناہی تنازعات چھوڑ دیتی ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: يؤكد الله أن مخاصمة أهل النار حق مطلق - سيتنازعون ويلوم بعضهم بعضاً بالفعل.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: جهنم تدمر كل رفقة ووحدة، تاركةً فقط كراهية متبادلة ونزاعاً لا نهاية له بين سكانها.

concepts.title: Divine Truth
concepts.coreInsight: The phrase 'Indeed, that is truth' (inna dhalika la-haqq) emphasizes that these descriptions of Hell are not metaphorical but reality.
concepts.whyItMatters: Allah's warnings about the Hereafter are not exaggerations or parables - they are literal truths we must prepare for.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: جملہ 'بیشک یہ سچ ہے' (ان ذالک لحق) اس بات پر زور دیتا ہے کہ جہنم کی یہ تفصیلات تمثیلی نہیں بلکہ حقیقت ہیں۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: آخرت کے بارے میں اللہ کی تنبیہات مبالغہ یا تمثیلیں نہیں - یہ حقیقی سچائیاں ہیں جن کے لیے ہمیں تیار ہونا چاہیے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: تؤكد عبارة 'إن ذلك لحق' أن هذه الأوصاف لجهنم ليست مجازية بل حقيقة.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: تحذيرات الله عن الآخرة ليست مبالغات أو أمثال - إنها حقائق حرفية يجب أن نستعد لها.

concepts.title: Social Collapse
concepts.coreInsight: The quarreling of Hell's people represents total social breakdown - all earthly bonds and loyalties are dissolved in suffering.
concepts.whyItMatters: Relationships built without Allah at their center cannot survive ultimate trials - only faith-based bonds endure.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: جہنمیوں کا جھگڑنا مکمل سماجی ٹوٹ پھوٹ کی نمائندگی کرتا ہے - تمام دنیوی تعلقات اور وفاداریاں عذاب میں ختم ہو جاتی ہیں۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: وہ تعلقات جو اللہ کو مرکز میں رکھے بغیر بنائے گئے ہوں حتمی آزمائشوں میں زندہ نہیں رہ سکتے - صرف ایمان پر مبنی بندھن برقرار رہتے ہیں۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: تمثل مخاصمة أهل النار انهياراً اجتماعياً تاماً - تذوب جميع الروابط والولاءات الدنيوية في المعاناة.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: العلاقات المبنية دون جعل الله في مركزها لا يمكنها النجاة من المحن القصوى - فقط الروابط القائمة على الإيمان تدوم.

64.layer4: Both Shia and Sunni commentators agree that this verse affirms the literal reality of the quarreling in Hell. Ibn Kathir states that the phrase 'inna dhalika la-haqqun' is God's confirmation that everything described will actually occur. Qurtubi emphasizes that it refutes those who allegorize Hell's descriptions. Razi notes that it serves to frighten the believers away from sin and warn the disbelievers while they still have opportunity to repent. The interpretive difference lies primarily in emphasis rather than substance. Shia scholars like Tabatabai tend to emphasize the psychological and social dimensions of Hell's torment alongside the physical, drawing on narrations from the Ahlul Bayt that describe the spiritual states of Hell's inhabitants. Sunni scholars tend to focus more on the physical punishments while acknowledging the psychological aspects. Both traditions agree that Hell is real, eternal for the disbelievers, and characterized by both physical and mental suffering. Both also agree that the purpose of these descriptions is not to satisfy curiosity but to motivate righteous action and sincere repentance. The Quran's vivid depictions of Hell's reality serve as mercy, warning humanity while there is still time to change course and seek God's forgiveness.
64.layer4_urdu: شیعہ اور سنی دونوں مفسرین اس بات پر متفق ہیں کہ یہ آیت جہنم میں جھگڑے کی لفظی حقیقت کی تصدیق کرتی ہے۔ ابن کثیر کہتے ہیں کہ عبارت "ان ذلک لحق" اللہ کی تصدیق ہے کہ جو کچھ بیان کیا گیا ہے وہ واقعی واقع ہوگا۔ قرطبی اس بات پر زور دیتے ہیں کہ یہ ان لوگوں کی تردید کرتی ہے جو جہنم کی تفصیلات کو علامتی بناتے ہیں۔ رازی نوٹ کرتے ہیں کہ یہ مومنین کو گناہ سے ڈرانے اور کافروں کو خبردار کرنے کے لیے کام کرتی ہے جب کہ انہیں ابھی توبہ کا موقع ہے۔ تشریحی فرق بنیادی طور پر زور میں ہے: شیعہ روایات خاص طور پر اس حقیقت کو ان لوگوں پر لاگو کرتی ہیں جنہوں نے اہل بیت پر ظلم کیا، جبکہ سنی ذرائع عام طور پر تمام کافروں اور گناہگاروں پر توجہ مرکوز کرتے ہیں۔
64.layer4_ar: يتفق مفسِّرو الشيعة والسنة على أن هذه الآية تُثبت واقعية التخاصم في النار إثباتاً قاطعاً. فيُبيِّن ابن كثير أن عبارة «إن ذلك لحقٌّ» هي تصديق الله على أن كل ما وُصف سيقع فعلاً. ويُشدِّد القرطبي على أنها ترد على من يُرمِّز أوصاف النار. ويُلاحِظ الرازي أنها تُخيف المؤمنين من الذنب وتُنذر الكافرين في حين لا يزال أمامهم فرصة للتوبة. والاختلاف التفسيري يقع في النبرة لا في الجوهر؛ فعلماء الشيعة كالطباطبائي يُميلون إلى التشديد على الأبعاد النفسية والاجتماعية لعذاب النار إلى جانب الجسدية، مستنيرين بروايات أهل البيت في أحوال أهل النار الروحية. بينما يُركِّز علماء السنة على العذاب الجسدي مع إقرارهم بالجانب النفسي. ويتفق التراثان على أن النار حقيقة واقعة وأبدية للكافرين وتجمع بين معاناة جسدية ونفسية. ويتفقان أيضاً على أن الغاية من هذه الأوصاف ليست إشباع الفضول بل الباعث على الصلاح وإخلاص التوبة. وتُعد الأوصاف القرآنية الحية للنار ضرباً من الرحمة الإلهية تُنذر البشرية في حين لا يزال بإمكانهم تغيير مسارهم والتوجه إلى مغفرة الله.
64.layer1: Verse 64 is a divine declaration that closes the scene of the disputing inhabitants of Hellfire and confirms its reality: 'Indeed, that is truth - the quarreling of the people of the Fire.' After the vivid and emotionally charged dialogue of the previous verses - the followers cursing their leaders, the leaders turning on the followers, the mutual bewilderment about the absent believers, and the agonizing self-questioning about their mockery - Allah intervenes with this declarative statement to confirm that what has just been described is not allegory or parable but absolute truth. The Arabic word 'haqq' means truth in its most definitive and uncompromising sense. What the Quran has portrayed is what will literally happen. The 'khisam,' meaning quarreling, dispute, or contention, refers specifically to the bitter arguments and mutual recriminations that will characterize the social reality of Hellfire. This verse is notable because it breaks the narrative to deliver a direct divine authentication of the scenes described. It functions as a kind of divine stamp of verification: everything you have just witnessed in these verses is true and will come to pass exactly as described. For the believer reading or hearing these verses, this divine confirmation serves as an urgent wake-up call. The social bonds formed through shared sinfulness and mutual misguidance in this world will not hold together in the Hereafter. Instead, they will shatter into bitter accusation. Those who thought they had powerful allies in their rejection of the truth will find those very allies transformed into their most virulent accusers. The verse underscores the foolishness of placing trust and loyalty in anything other than the path of Allah.
64.layer2: Imam Tabari in his Jami al-Bayan explains that this verse functions as a divine attestation to the reality of the scenes described. He notes that Allah uses the emphatic particle 'inna' (indeed) and the definitive 'haqq' (truth) together to leave absolutely no room for doubt about the factual nature of what has been described. Tabari draws on this verse to affirm the Islamic theological principle that the Quranic descriptions of the Hereafter are not symbolic or metaphorical but literally true in a manner that befits the majesty of the unseen realm. Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir records the view of Ibn Abbas and other companions and their students that this verse serves as a rhetorical seal on the preceding narrative, closing the scene with divine authority. He notes that the specific word 'takhsum' (quarreling, disputation) used here is striking because it implies the contentious and litigious nature of these arguments - not mere expressions of regret but active accusations and counter-accusations. Ibn Kathir connects this to the broader Quranic truth that the social dynamics of disbelief - the bonds of mutual sin, the hierarchies of corruption - will be fully exposed and destroyed in the Hereafter. Imam Qurtubi uses this verse to address those who might treat Quranic descriptions of the Hereafter as figurative, firmly establishing the orthodox Sunni position that these descriptions represent real events and real states. Al-Razi reflects in Mafatih al-Ghayb that the use of 'haqq' here is theologically weighty, representing Allah bearing witness to the truth of the scene described, which elevates the moral urgency of the warning.
64.layer3: Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran writes with characteristic force about this verse, noting that the divine confirmation of the quarreling of the people of Hell is one of the most sobering affirmations in the Quran. Allah does not merely narrate what will happen and leave it open to interpretation - He explicitly says: this is truth. Qutb reflects that this verse should strike fear into the heart of anyone who is currently engaged in relationships of mutual sinfulness, anyone following leaders of misguidance, or anyone who thinks that the bonds of shared worldly interest will provide any shelter in the Hereafter. Those bonds will not merely dissolve - they will invert into the most intense enmity. Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir draws attention to the way this verse creates a structural pause in the surah, transitioning from the scene of Hell's quarreling to the affirmation of monotheism in the very next verse. He notes that this juxtaposition is deliberate: after the terrifying picture of what awaits those who follow falsehood, the surah pivots immediately to the antidote, which is the declaration of pure tawhid. Ibn Uthaymeen emphasized in his teachings that Muslims must regularly reflect on Quranic scenes of the Hereafter as a spiritual discipline. The confirmation in this verse that 'this is truth' is meant to make those scenes feel real and present to the reader, not distant and theoretical. In contemporary Muslim life, where materialistic culture tends to make the Hereafter feel abstract and remote, this verse insists on its concrete, unalterable reality as the most important frame of reference for all human choices.

concepts.title: Warner's Role
concepts.coreInsight: Allah commands the Prophet to declare he is only a warner (mundhir), emphasizing the simplicity and clarity of his mission.
concepts.whyItMatters: The Prophet's role is to deliver the message clearly, not to force belief - guidance is Allah's domain, warning is the messenger's duty.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: اللہ نبی کو حکم دیتا ہے کہ وہ اعلان کریں کہ وہ صرف متنبہ کرنے والے (منذر) ہیں، اپنے مشن کی سادگی اور وضاحت پر زور دیتے ہوئے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: نبی کا کردار پیغام کو واضح طور پر پہنچانا ہے، ایمان پر مجبور کرنا نہیں - ہدایت اللہ کا دائرہ ہے، تنبیہ رسول کا فرض۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: يأمر الله النبي بأن يعلن أنه مجرد نذير، مؤكداً على بساطة ووضوح مهمته.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: دور النبي هو إيصال الرسالة بوضوح، وليس إجبار الناس على الإيمان - الهداية من شأن الله، والإنذار واجب الرسول.

concepts.title: Pure Monotheism
concepts.coreInsight: The declaration 'there is no deity except Allah, the One' (Allah al-Wahid) is the core message - absolute monotheism with no partners.
concepts.whyItMatters: Tawhid is the foundation of Islam - recognizing Allah's absolute oneness in essence, attributes, and worship is non-negotiable.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: اعلان 'اللہ کے سوا کوئی معبود نہیں، وہ واحد' (اللہ الواحد) بنیادی پیغام ہے - کسی شریک کے بغیر مطلق توحید۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: توحید اسلام کی بنیاد ہے - اللہ کی ذات، صفات اور عبادت میں مطلق وحدانیت کو تسلیم کرنا ناقابل مذاکرہ ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: إعلان 'لا إله إلا الله الواحد' هو الرسالة الجوهرية - التوحيد المطلق بلا شركاء.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: التوحيد أساس الإسلام - الاعتراف بوحدانية الله المطلقة في الذات والصفات والعبادة أمر غير قابل للتفاوض.

concepts.title: The Prevailing
concepts.coreInsight: Al-Qahhar (the Prevailing) describes Allah's absolute dominance over all creation - nothing can resist or oppose His will.
concepts.whyItMatters: Understanding Allah's overwhelming power should inspire both awe and submission - He is irresistible in His decree.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: القہار (غالب) تمام مخلوق پر اللہ کی مطلق بالادستی بیان کرتا ہے - کوئی چیز اس کی مرضی کا مقابلہ یا مزاحمت نہیں کر سکتی۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: اللہ کی زبردست قوت کو سمجھنا خوف اور تسلیم دونوں کو متاثر کرنا چاہیے - وہ اپنے حکم میں ناقابل مزاحمت ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: القهار يصف هيمنة الله المطلقة على جميع الخلق - لا شيء يمكنه مقاومة أو معارضة مشيئته.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: فهم قوة الله الساحقة يجب أن يلهم الرهبة والخضوع - إنه لا يُقاوم في قضائه.

65.layer4: Both Shia and Sunni scholars agree on the fundamental interpretation of this verse regarding the Prophet's role as warner and the centrality of tawhid. Ibn Kathir explains that 'mundhir' means the Prophet's duty is to convey the message clearly, after which each person bears responsibility for their response. Qurtubi emphasizes the two divine attributes mentioned, explaining 'al-Wahid' as absolute oneness and 'al-Qahhar' as overwhelming dominance over all creation. Razi provides extensive theological analysis of divine unity, consistent with the Shia emphasis on tawhid. The difference lies in how each tradition develops these concepts. Shia theology, particularly as articulated by scholars like Tabatabai, tends to emphasize the absolute transcendence of God and the inadequacy of all conceptualizations to capture divine reality. This approach, influenced by figures like Imam Ali's teachings, produces a strongly apophatic (negative) theology that emphasizes what God is not rather than what He is. Sunni theology, while affirming divine transcendence, tends to balance apophatic and cataphatic (positive) approaches. Both traditions agree that true tawhid must inform all aspects of life and that the Prophet's role as warner establishes human accountability. Both also affirm that these are not merely theoretical concepts but practical realities that should transform how believers live, worship, and interact with the world.
65.layer4_urdu: شیعہ اور سنی دونوں علماء نبی کے کردار کو خبردار کرنے والے اور توحید کی مرکزیت کے بارے میں اس آیت کی بنیادی تشریح پر متفق ہیں۔ ابن کثیر وضاحت کرتے ہیں کہ "منذر" کا مطلب ہے کہ نبی کا فرض پیغام کو واضح طور پر پہنچانا ہے، جس کے بعد ہر شخص اپنے جواب کی ذمہ داری رکھتا ہے۔ قرطبی مذکور دو الہی صفات پر زور دیتے ہیں، "الواحد" کو مطلق یکتائی اور "القہار" کو تمام مخلوقات پر غالب تسلط کے طور پر وضاحت کرتے ہوئے۔ رازی وسیع الہیاتی تجزیہ فراہم کرتے ہیں۔ شیعہ اور سنی تشریحات کے درمیان فرق بنیادی طور پر اطلاق میں ہے، شیعہ روایات اس آیت کو امامت کے تصور سے جوڑتی ہیں۔
65.layer4_ar: يتفق علماء الشيعة والسنة في تفسير هذه الآية إجمالاً فيما يتعلق بدور النبي منذراً ومحورية التوحيد. فيُبيِّن ابن كثير أن «منذر» يعني أن واجب النبي هو إيصال الرسالة بياناً ثم يتحمل كل فرد مسؤولية استجابته. ويُشدِّد القرطبي على الصفتين الإلهيتين مُفسِّراً «الواحد» بالوحدانية المطلقة و«القهار» بالسيطرة الساحقة على كل الخلق. ويقدِّم الرازي تحليلاً لاهوتياً مستفيضاً للوحدانية الإلهية يتسق مع التأكيد الشيعي على التوحيد. ويكمن الاختلاف في أسلوب توسيع كل تراث لهذه المفاهيم؛ فلاهوت الشيعة لا سيما على النحو الذي صاغه علماء كالطباطبائي يُميل إلى التشديد على مطلق تعالي الله وعلى قصور كل التصورات عن استيعاب الحقيقة الإلهية. وهذا المنهج المتأثر بتعاليم الإمام علي عليه السلام ينتج لاهوتاً سلبياً راسخاً يُعرِّف الله بما ليس عليه لا بما هو عليه. بينما يوازن لاهوت السنة بين المنهجين السلبي والإيجابي. ويتفق التراثان على أن التوحيد الحق ينبغي أن يتشرَّب كل جوانب الحياة وأن دور النبي منذراً يُثبت المسؤولية الإنسانية. ويتفقان كذلك على أن هذه ليست مفاهيم نظرية مجردة بل حقائق عملية ينبغي أن تُحوِّل طريقة إيمان المؤمنين وعبادتهم وتفاعلهم مع العالم من حولهم.
65.layer1: Verse 65 marks a pivotal transition in the surah, shifting from the terrifying scenes of Hellfire and its quarreling inhabitants to a direct and commanding declaration addressed through the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, to all of humanity. Allah instructs the Prophet to say: 'I am only a warner, and there is not any deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing.' This verse encapsulates two of the most fundamental truths of Islam in a single, powerful statement. The first is the nature of the Prophet's mission: he is 'mundhir,' a warner. This is not a limitation but a precise description of the prophetic function, which is to convey the message of divine guidance, warn of consequences, and leave the choice to human beings. The second is the core creed of Islam: there is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone. The two divine names invoked here are 'al-Wahid' meaning the One, the Unique, the Singular, and 'al-Qahhar' meaning the Prevailing, the Irresistible, the Overwhelming. Al-Wahid affirms the absolute uniqueness of Allah - there is no partner, no equal, no rival. Al-Qahhar affirms His absolute sovereignty - He subdues all things, all wills, all powers are subjugated beneath His authority. The juxtaposition of these two names after the scenes of Hell is deeply meaningful: no matter how powerful those leaders of misguidance seemed in this world, they are completely subdued by Allah. The verse thus connects the theological to the practical warning: the very God who will preside over the quarreling of the people of Hell is the One, the Prevailing, before whom all false gods and all worldly power are utterly insignificant.
65.layer2: Imam Tabari in Jami al-Bayan explains that the instruction for the Prophet to say 'I am only a warner' is a reaffirmation of prophetic methodology: the messenger's role is to deliver and warn, not to coerce. This was particularly significant in the Meccan context where the Prophet faced intense opposition and pressure, and this verse reassured him that his responsibility was conveyance and warning while Allah handled judgment and outcomes. Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir connects this verse to the recurring Quranic theme of prophetic limitation in role but not in truth - the Prophet was not a controller of hearts but a conveyor of revelation. Ibn Kathir notes that the divine names al-Wahid and al-Qahhar appear together here to emphasize the complete otherness and absolute authority of Allah. Al-Qahhar in particular, he explains, derives from the root qahara meaning to overcome and subdue completely, and it signifies that Allah dominates and overpowers all that exists, whether willingly or unwillingly. Imam Qurtubi uses this verse to establish a foundational point in Islamic theology: the Prophet's declaration of being 'only a warner' eliminates any basis for the veneration or deification of prophets. The Prophet is the greatest of human beings but he is a human being, a servant and messenger, defined by his function of warning rather than by any share in divine authority. Al-Razi in Mafatih al-Ghayb provides a detailed philosophical analysis of the divine name al-Qahhar, explaining that it signifies the complete subjugation of all created beings to the divine will, making any claim to partnership with Allah not merely wrong but cosmically absurd.
65.layer3: Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran writes that this verse is the spiritual axis around which the entire preceding passage revolves. After witnessing the scenes of Hell, the response offered by the Quran is not more description of torment but a clear and resounding declaration of tawhid. The solution to the tragedy of the people of Hell - who followed false leaders, mocked the righteous, and disputed bitterly in eternal torment - is contained in this verse: know that there is only one God, the One, the Prevailing, and align yourself with His messenger who is sent only as a warner. Qutb emphasizes that the name al-Qahhar is especially apposite here because it reminds every human being that no worldly power - no leader, no ideology, no social force - can resist or escape the dominion of Allah. Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir highlights that this verse initiates a new section of the surah dealing with the Prophet's role and the truth of monotheism, and that it sets up the subsequent verses about the story of iblis which deepen the understanding of how rebellion against Allah leads to the fate described in the Hellfire scenes. He notes that the command to the Prophet to declare himself as 'only a warner' has a rhetorical humility that is itself a manifestation of sincere servitude to Allah. Ibn Uthaymeen would often reflect on the name al-Qahhar in his lessons, noting that meditating on this name should produce in the believer both awe and comfort: awe because nothing can escape Allah's sovereignty, and comfort because the One who prevails over all things is the same One who is our Lord and protector. In the modern age of competing ideologies and overwhelming secular power, this declaration reasserts the primacy of divine authority over all human systems.

concepts.title: Lord of Everything
concepts.coreInsight: Allah is described as Lord of the heavens, earth, and everything between them - His sovereignty is absolute and comprehensive.
concepts.whyItMatters: No aspect of existence is outside Allah's dominion - He is the Creator and Sustainer of all realms, visible and invisible.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: اللہ کو آسمانوں، زمین اور ان کے درمیان ہر چیز کے رب کے طور پر بیان کیا گیا ہے - اس کی حاکمیت مطلق اور جامع ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: وجود کا کوئی پہلو اللہ کی حکومت سے باہر نہیں - وہ تمام دائروں، مرئی اور غیر مرئی کا خالق اور پروردگار ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: يُوصف الله بأنه رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما - سيادته مطلقة وشاملة.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: لا يوجد جانب من الوجود خارج سلطان الله - إنه الخالق والمدبر لجميع العوالم، المرئية وغير المرئية.

concepts.title: Exalted in Might
concepts.coreInsight: Al-Aziz (the Exalted in Might) signifies Allah's invincibility and honor - He is beyond any weakness or defeat.
concepts.whyItMatters: Trusting in Allah's might provides security - no force in creation can overcome His power or frustrate His plans.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: العزیز (صاحب عزت اور قوت) اللہ کی ناقابل شکست اور عزت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے - وہ کسی بھی کمزوری یا شکست سے بالاتر ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: اللہ کی قوت پر بھروسہ سکون فراہم کرتا ہے - مخلوق میں کوئی طاقت اس کی قدرت پر غالب یا اس کے منصوبوں کو ناکام نہیں کر سکتی۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: العزيز يدل على منعة الله وعزته - إنه فوق أي ضعف أو هزيمة.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: الثقة في قوة الله توفر الأمان - لا قوة في الخلق يمكنها التغلب على قدرته أو إحباط خططه.

concepts.title: Perpetual Forgiver
concepts.coreInsight: Al-Ghaffar (the Perpetual Forgiver) emphasizes Allah's endless capacity to forgive - no matter how many sins, He can pardon them all.
concepts.whyItMatters: This divine attribute offers hope to all sinners - sincere repentance is always accepted, and Allah's mercy exceeds His wrath.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: الغفار (ہمیشہ بخشنے والا) اللہ کی لامحدود بخشش کی صلاحیت پر زور دیتا ہے - کتنے ہی گناہ ہوں، وہ سب کو معاف کر سکتا ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: یہ الہی صفت تمام گناہگاروں کو امید دیتی ہے - مخلصانہ توبہ ہمیشہ قبول ہوتی ہے، اور اللہ کی رحمت اس کے غضب سے بڑھ کر ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: الغفار يؤكد قدرة الله اللامحدودة على المغفرة - مهما كثرت الذنوب، يمكنه أن يغفرها جميعاً.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: هذه الصفة الإلهية تمنح الأمل لجميع المذنبين - التوبة الصادقة تُقبل دائماً، ورحمة الله تتجاوز غضبه.

concepts.title: Balanced Attributes
concepts.coreInsight: The pairing of Al-Aziz (Mighty) with Al-Ghaffar (Forgiver) shows Allah's perfect balance - He is both powerful and merciful.
concepts.whyItMatters: Understanding both attributes prevents extremes - we neither despair of His mercy nor become complacent about His justice.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: العزیز (قوت والا) کا الغفار (بخشنے والے) کے ساتھ جوڑا اللہ کا کامل توازن ظاہر کرتا ہے - وہ طاقتور بھی ہے اور مہربان بھی۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: دونوں صفات کو سمجھنا انتہا پسندی سے روکتا ہے - ہم نہ اس کی رحمت سے مایوس ہوتے ہیں اور نہ اس کے انصاف کے بارے میں لاپرواہ۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: الجمع بين العزيز والغفار يُظهر التوازن الكامل لله - إنه قوي ورحيم في آن واحد.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: فهم كلا الصفتين يمنع التطرف - لا نيأس من رحمته ولا نتهاون بشأن عدالته.

66.layer4: Sunni and Shia scholars unanimously agree on the interpretation of this verse and its theological implications. Ibn Kathir explains that 'Rabb al-samawati wa al-ardi' establishes God's ownership and management of all creation. Qurtubi emphasizes the combination of 'al-Aziz' and 'al-Ghaffar,' noting that God's power makes His forgiveness all the more magnificent, since He could destroy sinners but chooses to forgive them. Razi provides detailed analysis of divine attributes, explaining that they are not separate from God's essence but are ways of understanding His relationship to creation. The Shia perspective, as articulated by Tabatabai and other scholars, tends to emphasize divine transcendence more strongly, cautioning against anthropomorphizing these attributes. When we speak of God as 'Rabb,' 'Aziz,' or 'Ghaffar,' we are describing His actions toward creation, not implying that He possesses attributes in the way creatures do. Both traditions agree that contemplating these divine attributes should produce transformation in the believer—humility before His might, hope in His mercy, gratitude for His sustenance, and determination to live in accordance with His guidance. Both also agree that the pairing of divine might and mercy throughout the Quran is pedagogically intentional, designed to cultivate balanced spiritual states that lead to righteousness. The consensus is that these are not merely abstract theological concepts but practical realities that should inform how believers understand themselves, the universe, and their relationship to God.
66.layer4_urdu: سنی اور شیعہ علماء اس آیت کی تشریح اور اس کے الہیاتی مضمرات پر متفقہ طور پر متفق ہیں۔ ابن کثیر وضاحت کرتے ہیں کہ "رب السماوات والارض" تمام مخلوقات کی اللہ کی ملکیت اور انتظام قائم کرتا ہے۔ قرطبی "العزیز" اور "الغفار" کے امتزاج پر زور دیتے ہیں، یہ نوٹ کرتے ہوئے کہ اللہ کی طاقت اس کی بخشش کو اور بھی شاندار بناتی ہے، کیونکہ وہ گناہگاروں کو تباہ کر سکتا ہے لیکن انہیں معاف کرنے کا انتخاب کرتا ہے۔ رازی الہی صفات کا تفصیلی تجزیہ فراہم کرتے ہیں، وضاحت کرتے ہوئے کہ وہ الگ الگ نہیں بلکہ ایک دوسرے کے ساتھ مربوط ہیں۔ دونوں روایات اس بات پر متفق ہیں کہ یہ آیت مومنین کو خوف اور امید کے درمیان توازن برقرار رکھنے کی تعلیم دیتی ہے۔
66.layer4_ar: يتفق علماء السنة والشيعة اتفاقاً تاماً على دلالة هذه الآية وما تنطوي عليه من أبعاد عقدية. فابن كثير يُبيِّن أن «رب السماوات والأرض» يُثبت ملكية الله وإدارته لجميع الخليقة. ويُلاحظ القرطبي أن الجمع بين «العزيز» و«الغفار» يُبرز عظمة المغفرة الإلهية، إذ كان سبحانه قادراً على تدمير العصاة لكنه يختار المغفرة فضلاً ورحمة. ويُقدِّم فخر الدين الرازي تحليلاً دقيقاً للصفات الإلهية مُبيِّناً أنها ليست منفصلة عن ذاته بل هي أوجه تعامله مع الخلق. أما التفسير الشيعي كما يصوغه الطباطبائي وسواه فيُشدِّد على التنزيه والتعالي الإلهي محذِّراً من تشبيه هذه الصفات بما هو معهود من الصفات البشرية؛ فحين نقول الله «رب» أو «عزيز» أو «غفار» فإننا نصف أفعاله تجاه الخلق لا ذاته كما تُوصف الكائنات. ويتفق التراثان على أن التأمل في هذه الصفات الإلهية ينبغي أن يُحوِّل المؤمن تحويلاً حقيقياً؛ تواضعاً أمام عزته ورجاءً في رحمته وشكراً على إمداده وعزماً على العيش وفق هدايته.
66.layer1: Verse 66 of Surah Sad presents one of the most majestic and comprehensive descriptions of Allah's sovereignty found in the Quran. The verse declares that the one God being affirmed throughout this surah is the Lord of the heavens, the earth, and everything that exists between them. The Arabic word Rabb carries deep meaning beyond the simple word 'Lord' — it denotes the Sustainer, the Master, the One who nurtures and governs all of creation at every moment. Nothing in the vast expanse of the universe falls outside His dominion. Two powerful divine names are then paired in a profoundly meaningful way: al-Aziz, the Almighty whose power none can resist or overcome, and al-Ghaffar, the Perpetual Forgiver who forgives again and again without limit. The pairing of absolute might with boundless forgiveness is a deliberate theological statement — the same God who has total power over His creation is also the most merciful and forgiving to those who turn back to Him. This verse appears in the closing section of Surah Sad, which is a Meccan surah revealed during a period of intense opposition to the Prophet Muhammad. The Quraysh of Mecca rejected the message of monotheism, so this verse serves as a reminder that the one true God who demands their worship is also the sustainer of everything they see around them. The practical lesson is that awareness of Allah's lordship should naturally cultivate both reverence of His might and hope in His forgiveness, and the believer should never fall into despair no matter how great their sins.
66.layer2: Imam al-Tabari in his Jami al-Bayan notes that verse 66 follows directly from the Prophet's declaration in verse 65 that there is no god but Allah, the One, the Dominant. Allah then affirms His comprehensive lordship — Rabb al-samawat wa-l-ard wa-ma baynahuma — as a logical completion of the concept of tawhid. Everything that exists is under His Rububiyyah, meaning His ownership, governance, and sustaining power. Al-Tabari links the name al-Aziz (the Almighty) to the idea that this God is invincible and cannot be overcome by any who refuse to worship Him, making polytheism not only false but utterly futile. Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim comments on the beautiful tension between al-Aziz and al-Ghaffar, noting that Allah could punish all transgressors instantly by virtue of His might, yet He is al-Ghaffar — He covers and forgives the sins of those who repent. Ibn Kathir notes that this divine name al-Ghaffar is on the pattern of great frequency and repetition in Arabic, indicating that Allah's forgiveness is not a one-time occurrence but a continual, habitual attribute. Imam al-Qurtubi in his al-Jami li-Ahkam al-Quran highlights the linguistic connection between al-Ghaffar and the word mighfar, a helmet that covers the head, suggesting that Allah's forgiveness literally covers and conceals the sins of the repentant believer so they are no longer exposed. This verse thus affirms two pillars of Islamic theology simultaneously: the transcendent power of Allah that demands submission, and the divine mercy that makes repentance always worthwhile.
66.layer3: Wahbah al-Zuhayli in his al-Tafsir al-Munir draws attention to the theological architecture of this verse, observing that the pairing of al-Aziz and al-Ghaffar is not accidental. Might without mercy would be terrifying, and mercy without might would be without authority — but together these names present the complete and balanced picture of the divine nature as Islam understands it. Al-Zuhayli notes that this verse serves as a corrective to two dangerous extremes in human religiosity: excessive fear that leads to hopelessness, and excessive confidence that leads to complacency about sin. Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran reflects on how the scope of Allah's lordship described here — covering the heavens, the earth, and all that is between them — is an invitation to contemplate the universe as a sign of divine sovereignty. Modern cosmology with its discovery of billions of galaxies only deepens rather than diminishes this sense of awe. Every star, every atom, every moment of time falls under the Rububiyyah described in this verse. Sheikh Ibn Uthaymeen emphasized in his lessons that the believer who truly internalizes Allah's being al-Aziz will never feel humiliated before any created being, because the only true might belongs to Allah. And the believer who internalizes Allah's being al-Ghaffar will always maintain hope and return to repentance, no matter how many times they fall. This verse thus provides the psychological and spiritual foundation for a life of dignified servitude to Allah combined with ongoing renewal through sincere repentance.

concepts.title: Great News
concepts.coreInsight: Allah calls the message of Islam 'great news' (naba'un azim) - the most important announcement in human history.
concepts.whyItMatters: The Quran and its core message deserve our utmost attention - this is not trivial information but news of cosmic significance.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: اللہ اسلام کے پیغام کو 'عظیم خبر' (نبا عظیم) قرار دیتا ہے - انسانی تاریخ کا سب سے اہم اعلان۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: قرآن اور اس کا بنیادی پیغام ہماری انتہائی توجہ کے مستحق ہیں - یہ معمولی معلومات نہیں بلکہ کائناتی اہمیت کی خبر ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: يسمي الله رسالة الإسلام 'نبأ عظيم' - الإعلان الأهم في تاريخ البشرية.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: القرآن ورسالته الأساسية تستحق اهتمامنا الأقصى - هذه ليست معلومات تافهة بل خبر ذو أهمية كونية.

concepts.title: Divine Command
concepts.coreInsight: The command 'Say' (Qul) emphasizes that the Prophet speaks by divine instruction, not personal opinion or conjecture.
concepts.whyItMatters: The Quran is revelation, not philosophy - every word carries divine authority and must be received with reverence.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: حکم 'کہہ دو' (قل) اس بات پر زور دیتا ہے کہ نبی الہی ہدایت سے بولتے ہیں، ذاتی رائے یا قیاس سے نہیں۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: قرآن وحی ہے، فلسفہ نہیں - ہر لفظ الہی اتھارٹی رکھتا ہے اور احترام کے ساتھ قبول کیا جانا چاہیے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: الأمر 'قل' يؤكد أن النبي يتكلم بتوجيه إلهي، وليس برأي شخصي أو تخمين.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: القرآن وحي وليس فلسفة - كل كلمة تحمل سلطة إلهية ويجب تلقيها بتوقير.

concepts.title: Emphatic Importance
concepts.coreInsight: The word 'azim' (great/tremendous) indicates the message's magnitude - belief in Allah's oneness and the Hereafter is paramount.
concepts.whyItMatters: We must not trivialize or ignore this message - it concerns our eternal destiny and deserves serious contemplation.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: لفظ 'عظیم' (بہت بڑا/زبردست) پیغام کی وسعت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے - اللہ کی وحدانیت اور آخرت پر ایمان سب سے اہم ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: ہمیں اس پیغام کو معمولی نہیں سمجھنا یا نظر انداز نہیں کرنا چاہیے - یہ ہماری ابدی تقدیر سے تعلق رکھتا ہے اور سنجیدہ غور و فکر کا مستحق ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: كلمة 'عظيم' تشير إلى عظمة الرسالة - الإيمان بوحدانية الله والآخرة أمر بالغ الأهمية.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: يجب ألا نستهين بهذه الرسالة أو نتجاهلها - إنها تتعلق بمصيرنا الأبدي وتستحق تأملاً جاداً.

67.layer4: Sunni and Shia scholars agree that 'naba'un azim' refers to the momentous importance of the Quranic message. Ibn Kathir explains that it encompasses the entire message of Islam, particularly the doctrines of divine oneness, prophethood, and resurrection. Qurtubi emphasizes that the adjective 'azim' indicates this is the most significant information humans can receive. Razi provides extensive analysis of why this message deserves to be called 'great,' citing its content, source, and consequences. The Shia interpretation, following narrations from the Ahlul Bayt, tends to give specific emphasis to Wilayah—the divinely appointed leadership of the Prophet and Imams—as central to this great news. Tabatabai and other Shia scholars argue that without proper guidance in understanding and implementing the message, its greatness cannot be fully realized. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the necessity of divinely appointed Imams to guide the community. Sunni scholars generally interpret 'great news' more broadly without this specific emphasis on Imamate, though they acknowledge the importance of righteous leadership. Both traditions agree that the message's greatness demands serious engagement rather than indifference, and that turning away from it despite its obvious importance is a grave spiritual failing. Both also agree that this verse serves to elevate the status of the Quranic message above all other knowledge and information.
67.layer4_urdu: سنی اور شیعہ علماء اس بات پر متفق ہیں کہ "نباً عظیم" قرآنی پیغام کی اہم اہمیت کی طرف اشارہ کرتی ہے۔ ابن کثیر وضاحت کرتے ہیں کہ یہ اسلام کے پورے پیغام کو شامل کرتی ہے، خاص طور پر الہی یکتائی، نبوت اور قیامت کے عقائد۔ قرطبی اس بات پر زور دیتے ہیں کہ صفت "عظیم" اس بات کی نشاندہی کرتی ہے کہ یہ سب سے اہم معلومات ہے جو انسان حاصل کر سکتے ہیں۔ رازی وسیع تجزیہ فراہم کرتے ہیں کہ یہ پیغام "عظیم" کہلانے کا مستحق کیوں ہے، اس کے مواد، ذریعہ اور نتائج کا حوالہ دیتے ہوئے۔ شیعہ اور سنی تشریحات کے درمیان فرق اس میں ہے کہ شیعہ روایات خاص طور پر امامت کو اس عظیم خبر کا حصہ شامل کرتی ہیں۔
67.layer4_ar: يتفق علماء السنة والشيعة على أن «نبأ عظيم» يُشير إلى الأهمية القصوى للرسالة القرآنية. فابن كثير يُبيِّن أنها تشمل رسالة الإسلام في مجملها لا سيما مفاهيم التوحيد والنبوة والبعث. ويُؤكِّد القرطبي أن صفة «العظيم» تُشير إلى أن هذا أهم ما يُمكن أن يصل إلى الإنسان من المعلومات في حياته. ويُقدِّم الرازي تحليلاً واسعاً لوجه عظمة هذا النبأ مستعرضاً مضمونه ومصدره وعواقبه الأبدية. والتفسير الشيعي وفق ما يرويه أهل البيت يُولي اهتماماً خاصاً لعقيدة الولاية بوصفها محور هذا النبأ، مُقرِّراً أن القرآن دون دليل ربانيٍّ يُبيِّن مراده لا يمكن أن يُحقِّق الهداية المنشودة كمالاً. بينما يُفسِّر علماء السنة «النبأ العظيم» تفسيراً أشمل دون هذا التركيز الخاص على الإمامة. ويتفق التراثان على أن عظمة هذا النبأ تُوجب الانخراط الجاد في دراسته والعمل بمقتضاه لا التعامل معه باستهانة أو إعراض.
67.layer1: Verse 67 of Surah Sad is a brief but powerful declaration in which Allah instructs the Prophet Muhammad to say to the disbelievers: 'This is a momentous news.' The phrase naba un azim in Arabic means an announcement or piece of news that is of immense significance and gravity. The verse shifts in tone from the majestic description of Allah's lordship in verse 66 to a direct address to those who are turning away from the message of Islam. What is the 'momentous news'? Classical and modern scholars have offered several interpretations: it refers to the Quran itself, to the message of monotheism (tawhid), to the resurrection and the Day of Judgment, or to the account of the angels' dispute about Adam mentioned in the verses that follow. Many scholars hold that it refers primarily to the entire revelation and its consequences — the news that there is one God, that a Day of Accountability is coming, and that no intercession will save those who reject the truth. The verse is significant in its rhetorical strategy: instead of arguing at length against the disbelievers' objections, Allah simply instructs the Prophet to declare that this message is something momentous that they are ignoring at their own peril. The emphasis is on the weight and seriousness of the Quran itself, presented not as a debatable philosophical position but as a world-altering piece of news that demands a response. This verse calls every reader to examine how seriously they take the Quranic message in their own lives.
67.layer2: Imam al-Tabari in Jami al-Bayan records multiple views among the early Muslims and Companions regarding what naba un azim refers to. Some held that it is the Quran itself, while others said it refers to the Day of Resurrection and the accountability that comes with it. A third opinion, well-supported by the context of the surrounding verses, is that the 'momentous news' refers specifically to the dispute of the supreme assembly of angels over the creation of Adam — an event of cosmic significance introduced in verse 69. Al-Tabari notes that regardless of which specific referent is intended, the verse makes an overarching claim: the Quraysh are treating something of extraordinary cosmic importance as if it were beneath their consideration. Ibn Kathir in his tafsir agrees that the most likely referent is the overall message of Islam — the news of tawhid, prophethood, resurrection, and accountability — and he notes that the disbelievers 'turn away from it' as mentioned in verse 68, indicating their willful rejection rather than ignorance. Ibn Kathir draws a parallel to Surah al-Naba where the question 'About what are they asking one another?' opens a surah about the resurrection, suggesting that 'great news' in the Quran consistently points to matters of ultimate consequence — life, death, judgment, and eternity. Imam Fakhr al-Din al-Razi in his Mafatih al-Ghayb notes the rhetorical force of the brief declaration: its very brevity and directness communicates urgency, much like a herald announcing a king's proclamation.
67.layer3: Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran reflects on verse 67 with characteristic literary sensitivity, noting that the phrase 'momentous news' creates a sense of dramatic weight — the message of Islam is not a casual matter or a minor religious preference but a declaration that reshapes how one understands all of reality. Qutb emphasizes that the Quran presents itself as an event, a happening in human history, not merely a book. The news it brings — that God is one, that humans are accountable, that there is a life after death — changes everything if truly accepted. Wahbah al-Zuhayli in al-Tafsir al-Munir highlights the communicative function of the verse: by labeling the message as 'momentous news,' Allah is simultaneously affirming the importance of the Prophet's mission and indicting the disbelievers for their frivolous dismissal of something of ultimate seriousness. Modern commentators observe that in an age saturated with information and news, the challenge for Muslims is to internalize the Quran as naba un azim — news more important than any breaking headline — rather than treating it as mere cultural heritage. Sheikh Muhammad al-Sha'rawi reflected that true faith begins when a person feels the weight of what the Quran is announcing: not just religious information, but a life-altering, eternity-shaping message that requires a decisive response. The verse thus functions as a call to seriousness about the Quran in every generation.

concepts.title: Turning Away
concepts.coreInsight: Despite the greatness of the message, people turn away (mu'ridun) from it, choosing ignorance over guidance.
concepts.whyItMatters: Heedlessness is a spiritual disease - turning away from divine guidance leads to loss in this world and the next.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: پیغام کی عظمت کے باوجود، لوگ اس سے منہ موڑ لیتے (معرضون) ہیں، ہدایت کے بجائے جہالت کا انتخاب کرتے ہوئے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: غفلت ایک روحانی بیماری ہے - الہی رہنمائی سے منہ موڑنا اس دنیا اور اگلی دونوں میں نقصان کا باعث بنتا ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: رغم عظمة الرسالة، يعرض الناس عنها، مختارين الجهل على الهدى.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: الغفلة مرض روحي - الإعراض عن الهداية الإلهية يؤدي إلى الخسارة في الدنيا والآخرة.

concepts.title: Active Rejection
concepts.coreInsight: The term 'mu'ridun' implies active turning away, not passive ignorance - it's a deliberate choice to reject the truth.
concepts.whyItMatters: Many people know the truth but choose to ignore it for worldly reasons - this willful blindness increases accountability.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: اصطلاح 'معرضون' فعال طور پر منہ موڑنے کو ظاہر کرتی ہے، غیر فعال جہالت کو نہیں - یہ سچائی کو مسترد کرنے کا شعوری انتخاب ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: بہت سے لوگ سچائی کو جانتے ہیں لیکن دنیوی وجوہات کی بنا پر اسے نظر انداز کرنے کا انتخاب کرتے ہیں - یہ ارادی اندھا پن جوابدہی بڑھاتا ہے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: مصطلح 'معرضون' يعني الإعراض النشط، وليس الجهل السلبي - إنه اختيار متعمد لرفض الحق.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: كثير من الناس يعرفون الحق لكن يختارون تجاهله لأسباب دنيوية - هذا العمى المتعمد يزيد من المساءلة.

concepts.title: Direct Address
concepts.coreInsight: The use of 'you' (antum) makes this a direct confrontation - Allah addresses the rejecters personally and immediately.
concepts.whyItMatters: The Quran speaks to each reader directly - we cannot hide behind collective guilt but must examine our own response to truth.
concepts.coreInsight_urdu: لفظ 'تم' (انتم) کا استعمال اسے براہ راست مواجہہ بناتا ہے - اللہ منکرین کو ذاتی اور فوری طور پر مخاطب کرتا ہے۔
concepts.whyItMatters_urdu: قرآن ہر قاری سے براہ راست بات کرتا ہے - ہم اجتماعی قصور کے پیچھے نہیں چھپ سکتے بلکہ سچائی کے بارے میں اپنے ردعمل کا جائزہ لینا چاہیے۔
concepts.coreInsight_ar: استخدام 'أنتم' يجعل هذا مواجهة مباشرة - الله يخاطب الرافضين شخصياً وفورياً.
concepts.whyItMatters_ar: القرآن يتحدث إلى كل قارئ مباشرة - لا يمكننا الاختباء خلف الذنب الجماعي بل يجب أن نفحص استجابتنا الخاصة للحق.

68.layer4: Both Sunni and Shia commentators agree that this verse condemns the disbelievers' deliberate avoidance of the Quranic message despite its clear importance. Ibn Kathir explains that 'mu'ridun' (those who turn away) refers to those who hear the message but refuse to accept it, either through arrogance, attachment to worldly life, or blind following of tradition. Qurtubi notes that the verse applies both to the Prophet's contemporaries who rejected his message and to all subsequent generations who hear the Quran but fail to respond appropriately. Razi emphasizes the irrational nature of turning away from obviously important information, comparing it to someone who ignores a physician's diagnosis of a fatal but curable disease. The Shia interpretation, influenced by the Ahlul Bayt's teachings, tends to emphasize that 'i'rad' includes not just outright rejection but also partial engagement that falls short of full commitment. Tabatabai and other Shia scholars stress that genuine acceptance of the message requires both intellectual affirmation and practical implementation. Both traditions agree that this verse serves as both condemnation and invitation—condemnation of those who persist in turning away, invitation to those who recognize themselves in the description to change course. Both also emphasize that the verse's directness and clarity leave no excuse for continued heedlessness once it has been heard and understood.
68.layer4_urdu: سنی اور شیعہ دونوں مفسرین اس بات پر متفق ہیں کہ یہ آیت کافروں کے قرآنی پیغام سے جان بوجھ کر بچنے کو مذمت کرتی ہے اس کی واضح اہمیت کے باوجود۔ ابن کثیر وضاحت کرتے ہیں کہ "معرضون" (منہ موڑنے والے) ان لوگوں کی طرف اشارہ کرتے ہیں جو پیغام سنتے ہیں لیکن اسے قبول کرنے سے انکار کرتے ہیں، یا تو تکبر، دنیاوی زندگی سے وابستگی، یا روایت کی اندھی پیروی کے ذریعے۔ قرطبی نوٹ کرتے ہیں کہ آیت نبی کے عصری لوگوں پر لاگو ہوتی ہے جنہوں نے ان کے پیغام کو مسترد کیا اور بعد کی تمام نسلوں پر جو سچائی سے منہ موڑتی ہیں۔ رازی اس منہ موڑنے کی نفسیاتی جڑوں پر بحث کرتے ہیں۔ دونوں روایات اس بات پر متفق ہیں کہ یہ آیت خود جانچ اور توبہ کی دعوت ہے۔
68.layer4_ar: يتفق علماء السنة والشيعة على أن هذه الآية تذم الإعراض المتعمَّد عن الرسالة القرآنية رغم وضوحها البيِّن. فابن كثير يُبيِّن أن «المعرضون» هم الذين يسمعون الرسالة ثم يأبون قبولها إما كبراً أو تعلقاً بالدنيا أو تقليداً أعمى. ويُلاحظ القرطبي أن الآية تنطبق على معاصري النبي الذين رفضوا رسالته وعلى كل من سمع القرآن في كل العصور دون أن يستجيب له استجابة لائقة. ويُبرز الرازي اللامعقولية في تجاهل معلومة بالغة الأهمية مشبِّهاً ذلك بمن يتجاهل تشخيص الطبيب لمرض فتاك قابل للشفاء. والتفسير الشيعي بما وُرِّث من تعاليم أهل البيت يُشدِّد على أن «الإعراض» يشمل الانخراط الجزئي الذي يقصر عن الالتزام الكامل؛ فقبول الرسالة قبولاً حقيقياً يستلزم التصديق العقلي والتطبيق العملي معاً. ويتفق التراثان على أن الآية إدانة ودعوة في آنٍ معاً؛ إدانة لمن يُمادي في الإعراض ودعوة لمن يعرف نفسه في هذه الصورة أن يُسارع إلى تغيير مساره قبل فوات الأوان.
68.layer1: Verse 68 of Surah Sad continues directly from the declaration of verse 67 about the 'momentous news' by describing the response of the disbelievers to it: they turn away from it with indifference. The Arabic phrase 'antum anhu mu'ridun' means 'you are turning away from it' — indicating not just ignorance but an active, ongoing posture of rejection and avoidance.
